arxiv-2603-14569: Gadelrab, Kech and Cruz simulate how water changes the mechanics of Polyamide 6,6. The polymer is a key engineering plastic with strong hydrogen bonds. Water uptake shifts its glass transition and stiffness in practice. Atomistic simulations track that shift across water levels. At low water content, lone water molecules bind amide groups and stiffen chains. Past about 2.5 weight percent, water clusters break the bond network. The glass transition then drops sharply, and the modulus softens with heat and water.
arxiv-2603-14669: Park and Kang treat rendering as memory retrieval for embodied agents in RenderMem. What an agent can see depends on where it stands. Stored photos and object lists ground spatial claims poorly. RenderMem keeps a 3D scene model instead of fixed views. Queries trigger fresh renders from the viewpoint the question implies. Line-of-sight, visibility and occlusion can then be judged from any stance. The frame fits standard vision-language models with no changes. AI2-THOR tests show steady gains on viewpoint queries, they report.
arxiv-2603-15369: Hillairet and co-authors model contagious cyber events with a stochastic SIR model tied to firm growth. Firm size and growth in real data show heavy tails, and contagion depends on firm size and setting. Attack timing blends a Cox process for outside spread with a Bernoulli draw for spread from sister firms. Applied to LockBit attacks in mid 2024, the model covers 2,929 firms near Paris. It finds even odds that losses reach two days of revenue over a 100-day incident.
arxiv-2603-15569: Lahoti and co-authors present Mamba-3, a sequence model built from state space principles with inference speed as the design guide. Transformers pay quadratic compute and growing memory at generation time. Mamba-3 sharpens the recurrence from the state space view and adds a complex-valued state update for richer tracking. A multi-input, multi-output form lifts quality with no added decode delay. At 1.5 billion parameters, it beat the next best linear model on average downstream accuracy. It also matched Mamba-2 perplexity with half the state size.
arxiv-2603-15669: Jin and co-authors predict electron density with a Fourier Neural Operator. Density functional theory is exact enough for wide use but slow at scale. Their model learns a direct map from outside potentials to electron density. It skips atomic orbitals, basis sets, and handcrafted descriptors. Frequency-domain operator learning captures global interactions and long-range links. Training spanned many elements and molecular shapes. The model then hit unseen molecules with no retraining. The authors frame it as a fast route for screening work.
arxiv-2603-15769: Priestley and co-authors test whether the HCN line really traces star-forming gas. Galaxy surveys show HCN brightness tracking star formation rate almost linearly. Resolved cloud views suggest true star-forming gas sits at higher densities. The team ran radiative transfer on simulated magnetized clouds. HCN brightness stayed near flat across wide swings in star formation rate. The N2H+ line tracked the rate weakly and unevenly. The N2H+ to HCN ratio tracked dense gas fraction best. Galaxy-scale links come from averaging many clouds, they argue.
arxiv-2603-15969: Model, Ahmadi, and Vamvas build a language identifier for Romansh varieties. Romansh splits into regional idioms with patchy mutual understanding. No documented system split those idioms before this work. Rumantsch Grischun, a blended supra-regional form, joins the label set. Their SVM classifier trains for the multi-way idiom task. A fresh benchmark covers two text domains for scoring. Average in-domain accuracy reaches 97 percent, they report. Idiom-aware spell checks and translation tools can build on it. The classifier is public for reuse.
arxiv-2603-16169: Yalavarthi rebuilds Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation (CRAG) using only open tools. The original system used Google search and closed model weights. His version swaps in the Wikipedia API and the Phi-3-mini model. Tests on PopQA and ARC-Challenge show scores close to the original. He also runs the first SHAP analysis of CRAG's T5-based retrieval scorer. The scorer leans on named entity matches more than meaning. Code and results are public.
arxiv-2603-16369: Allu and co-authors study the Bohr phenomenon for operators on complex Banach spaces. They compute Bohr radii tied to four named maps. The maps are the Cesáro operator and the Bernardi integral operator. The list adds a beta-Cesáro operator and the discrete Fourier transform. All act on holomorphic mappings between two unit balls. The domain is the unit ball of a complex Banach space. The target is the closure of the unit polydisc.
arxiv-2603-16769: Yi and co-authors improve one-step generative image super-resolution with reinforcement learning. One-step models vary too little for standard training tricks, so the team adds a noise-aware diffusion model that can produce diverse outputs. An unequal-timestep scheme keeps the added noise from harming quality. Their GDPO method then scores groups of online samples against each other, in the spirit of preference learning. A reward function also weighs smooth and textured areas apart. Tests show the method lifts one-step super-resolution quality.
arxiv-2603-16869: Li and a large team introduce SegviGen, which turns a 3D generative model into a part segmentation tool. Older routes lift 2D priors into 3D and blur borders, or need huge labeled datasets. SegviGen instead uses the priors inside a pretrained generative model. It encodes a 3D asset and predicts colors that mark parts on a matched reconstruction. One framework covers interactive, full, and 2D-guided segmentation. The authors report gains of 40 percent on interactive and 15 percent on full segmentation, using only 0.32 percent of the labeled training data.
arxiv-2603-17069: Wang and co-authors build a privacy preserving fall detector for bathrooms, aimed at seniors living alone. Their system fuses radar motion data with floor vibration data. A Motion-Mamba branch reads long range motion patterns. An Impact-Griffin branch reads impact transients in the vibration signal. Fusion aligns the two streams and suppresses false alarms from dropped objects. The model runs in real time on a Raspberry Pi 4B. On their benchmark, it reached accuracy above 96 percent and cut latency sharply.
arxiv-2603-17269: Rema, Rubio López, and Herrera show that a molecular coating can switch on strong coupling in optical nanocavities. Quantum emitters near silver nanoparticles can couple strongly to dark multipole modes, but the bright dipole modes couple too weakly. Using macroscopic quantum electrodynamics theory, the authors show that a thin J-aggregate coating reshapes the local vacuum at dipole frequencies. The core shell structure forms a plexciton resonance. For quantum dot emitters near silver spheres of 20 nanometre radius, the coating turns plain exponential decay into Rabi oscillations.
arxiv-2603-17469: Fischer speeds up inference for hidden Markov models with Gaussian field effects. Such fields add spatial or trend structure, but they break the sparsity fast methods need. His modified forward algorithm restores a sparse Hessian for the model likelihood. Automatic differentiation and the Laplace approximation then scale to high dimensions. Simulations and two case studies, stellar flares and lion movement, show the approach works in practice.
arxiv-2603-17569: Ayday, Yang, and Ghoshdastidar study why graph transformers beat message-passing networks in theory. They take Gaussian process limits of three designs at infinite width and heads. Node and edge kernels then show how features and structure flow through attention layers. Graph transformers keep community signal and distinct node states even in deep layers, they prove. That trait blocks the oversmoothing that hurts older designs. Tests on real and synthetic graphs agree.
arxiv-2603-18069: Martins, Cardeira, and Oliveira present a control law for global position and heading tracking on SE(3). It serves underactuated vehicles with single-axis thrust, full torque, and strict input limits. A saturated position controller with two filters yields bounded attitude references. The inner loop pairs a saturated Rodrigues-based law with a hybrid path-lifting step. Proofs give robust global tracking, and simulations confirm the design.
arxiv-2603-18169: Menezes and Helayël-Neto bound a model with photon-photino oscillation from stellar physics. A Lorentz-violating fermionic condensate background mixes the photon with its supersymmetric partner. The mixing term appears naturally in a superspace and superfield treatment. They inspect the kinetic mixing matrix in a stellar setting. Solar data and an energy loss argument then set limits on the background strength.
arxiv-2603-18269: Sobah and D'Almeida prove that the four-velocity planar Broadwell model has one global solution, and just one. This small discrete model mimics the Boltzmann equation for gas flow out of balance. They treat the time-based problem on a box-shaped domain with set start and edge values. Fixed point tools plus sharp bounds keep the solution and its slopes in check for all time. The proof works in a class that lets slopes jump on a few planes at most.
arxiv-2603-18769: Friss and co-authors test whether air delivery of hydrogen cyanide limits prebiotic chemistry on rocky planets. Hydrogen cyanide feeds the RNA world picture. Warm little ponds could gather such molecules through wet-dry cycles. A one-dimensional atmospheric model compares air delivery with meteorite supply. Early Archean Earth serves as the baseline case. The team varies carbon-to-oxygen ratio, orbit distance, star type, and methane budget. Air delivery beats meteorite supply and stays robust. They conclude this molecule is likely not the bottleneck for early chemistry.
arxiv-2603-19469: Siu and co-authors build a formal frame for security in language model agents. The same act can be fine or a breach, based on who asked and why. They state four properties: task fit, action fit, source rights, and data isolation. Oracle checks then test if a run breaks any property. Known attacks, from prompt injection to memory poisoning, are recast as breaches of one or more properties. The aim is to end the blunt trade of utility for safety.
arxiv-2603-19569: Jiang and co-authors present hierNest, a framework for predicting hospital readmission risk. Patient groups differ widely by primary diagnosis, so one flat model fits poorly. The method uses the hierarchy of diagnoses grouped into major categories. Structured regularization lets related subgroups borrow strength from each other. Interpretability is kept at each level of the hierarchy. Simulations show better accuracy, above all for small subgroups. The team also applies the method to a large Medicare records data set.
arxiv-2603-19669: Manna and co-authors analyse prime order element graphs of finite Abelian groups. In this graph, group elements are vertices, joined when the product has prime order. The graph is connected when the group order is square-free. Other groups give several components, some matching graphs of smaller groups. The team studies traits like regularity and bipartiteness across components. Arranging elements in special orders reveals block structure in the adjacency matrix. That structure yields the characteristic polynomials and eigenvalues of the graphs.
arxiv-2603-19969: Ovide, Angles-Castillo, and Almudever route qubits in trapped-ion QCCD machines with parallelism in mind. QCCD designs link many trap zones and move ions between them for scaling. That transport can cost fidelity if done poorly. Their routing strategy adapts to both the algorithm's shape and the device layout. A scoring system with tunable weights balances transport cost against parallel work across traps. Across many benchmarks and layouts, the method cut transport overhead and raised execution fidelity. It beat leading routing tools in their tests.
arxiv-2603-20169: Shen and co-authors build EgoForge, a simulator that generates first-person video toward a stated goal. Egocentric video is hard: views swing fast, hands interact often, and intent stays hidden. Past methods need dense inputs like camera paths or long video prefixes. EgoForge starts from one egocentric image, a high-level instruction, and an optional outside view. Its GRAFT method refines whole trajectories with a diffusion process. Rewards for goal fit, timing, scene consistency, and looks steer the sampling. Tests show gains in semantic alignment and geometric stability.
arxiv-2603-20369: Sauliere and co-authors study how error correction in quantum channels fails as noise grows. A channel encodes logical information into a larger quantum space. They model channels as one-dimensional random noisy circuits with local gates. Noise can strike after encoding or during the encoding circuit itself. In the deep limit, random matrix theory predicts a sharp transition. Past a critical noise rate, encoded information is lost for good. Finite depth behavior differs by case, approaching perfect encoding at distinct rates.
arxiv-2603-20969: Vasudeva and co-authors study contextual recall, where a model uses paired examples in a prompt to recall facts in a new format. They build a synthetic setup where pretraining text links subjects, grammars, and attributes. Pretraining alone gives factual knowledge but not contextual recall. Fine tuning on a separate task that needs implicit inference triggers recall across all subjects. Low dimensional encodings of the shared attribute type form at the same time. They also give an attention only construction that mirrors the shift.
arxiv-2603-21369: Seth and co-authors look for signs that sparse random matrices fail to be ergodic. Such matrices model the Fock space graph of many-body systems, which is sparse by nature. They map where the ground state shifts from spread out to localized as sparsity varies. Short range energy correlations place the Anderson transition at the percolation limit of the graph. Energy moments and shifted kurtosis give the same threshold. Long range correlations point to a broad regime, inside the spread out phase, where the system is still not ergodic.
arxiv-2603-21569: Ohashi and Kudo enumerate a special family of algebraic curves: superspecial hyperelliptic curves of genus 5. Their chosen curves have automorphism groups containing three copies of the two-element cyclic group. Counts of superspecial curves are well understood only up to genus 3, with genus 4 partly covered by computational work. The authors build a feasible enumeration algorithm for their genus 5 family. Running it in Magma, they completed the count in every characteristic between 11 and 1000.
arxiv-2603-21969: Yang and co-authors image the spin polarization of KV2Se2O, a d-wave altermagnet metal. Altermagnets pair zero net magnetization with spin splitting that varies with momentum, breaking the old ferro-antiferro split. The team used spin-selective scanning tunneling microscopy with a topological insulator tip. Their images reveal momentum-dependent spin splitting set by crystal symmetry, with the d-wave form. The finding ties symmetry, band structure, and spin texture in one material. They offer it as a testbed for spintronics.
arxiv-2603-22069: Banerjee studies the centered isoperimetric inequality on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds with a warped product structure. At fixed volume, a geodesic ball at the pole has the least perimeter. Banerjee draws out several necessary conditions tied to the warped structure. Some echo effects found earlier by Brendle. He also gives a sufficient condition for the inequality to hold. With a new isoperimetric quotient, he improves the classical Cheeger inequality for a broad class of manifolds. He ends with a lower bound for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of such balls.
arxiv-2603-22469: Saccani and co-authors tackle a hidden risk in updating neural controllers while a system runs. Swapping one stabilizing policy for another can itself break stability. They model each controller as an operator with bounded gain and derive rules for safe updates. Two schemes follow: updates on a fixed schedule, and updates triggered by the state. Either way, the closed loop stays stable after any number of swaps. The team shows gains over static and naive updating on nonlinear test systems.
arxiv-2603-22769: Starko and Kirchner study collision paths that can trigger interatomic Coulombic decay in argon dimers. A helium ion hits the dimer, and electron removal or excitation opens the decay route. Their model treats atoms and electrons as independent units. They track the dimer at fixed bond length and vary impact energy widely. A determinantal analysis sorts the excitation channels. The authors find the 3d excited state dominates the decay route. Other states from 4s to 4f also contribute. Helium-plus projectiles give a strong route at low impact energy.
arxiv-2603-23569: Xu tracks the rise of equal-contribution authorship in papers. Two or more authors now often share credit as equals on the byline. He mines about 480,000 records from PubMed and PMC across 2010 to 2024. The share of such papers climbs after 2017, in mega-journals and small ones alike. Median journal share rose from a fifth in 2015 to over 30 percent in 2024. China supplies the largest slice of these contributions. Equal tags cluster near the first-author slot, not the middle or end.
arxiv-2603-24469: Kenworthy and co-authors describe a coronagraph for the ERIS instrument on the Very Large Telescope. The grating vector apodizing phase plate design aims to block starlight so faint companions can be seen. They cover the design, lab manufacture, and on-sky testing across filters from K to L band. The optic hits its transmission targets, 90 percent in K band and 60 percent in L band, and reaches its designed raw contrast. Detector noise, though, blocks the post-processed contrast goal, so they recommend it for known companions at known positions.
arxiv-2603-24569: Moscati and co-authors lay out the evaluation plan for the POLY-SIM Grand Challenge 2026. The challenge targets speaker identification when audio-visual data is incomplete and speakers switch languages. Real systems often lose the visual stream to occlusion, camera failure, or privacy limits. The plan describes the dataset, task formulation, evaluation protocol, and a baseline model. Its aim is a standard benchmark that pushes methods to use partial multimodal input well. Performance must hold across languages, not just in clean, complete recordings.
arxiv-2603-24669: Fornal considers a universe with three-torus topology that starts out empty of matter and radiation. Before inflation, its evolution is driven only by Casimir energies, with a radiation-like equation of state. Under natural assumptions, with the right balance of fermions and bosons, such a universe can begin at Planck size at the Planck time. With typical inflation and reheating parameters, it would now span several Hubble radii. That size matches a hint from a cosmic microwave background anomaly,.
arxiv-2603-24769: Könyves-Tóth and co-authors estimate the distance to the galaxy NGC 6951 using two supernova siblings. Siblings, supernovae in the same host, calibrate distance methods with lower systematic error. The pair is a Type IIP event from 2020 and a Type Ib event from 2021. Photometry came from two Hungarian telescopes, and spectra from public archives. Both distances use the expanding photosphere method, which links angular size, physical radius, and photosphere velocity. The estimates agree near 25 megaparsecs, giving a firmer distance for a galaxy that has hosted five supernovae.
arxiv-2603-25269: Ocampo, Caselli, and Ceolin tackle hate posts that hide behind fact-like claims. Such posts force moderators to judge both harm and truth, which doubles the work. The team releases WSF-ARG+, the first dataset that pairs hate speech with check-worthiness labels. Their annotation loop puts a language model beside human raters to mark which claims merit a check. Twelve open models were tried in that loop. Human checks show the loop cuts effort without hurting quality. Adding the labels lifts hate detection scores as well.
arxiv-2603-25369: Cristoferi, Deutsch, and Pignatelli study phase separation models with rough, place-dependent energy wells. The Cahn-Hilliard functional describes how two liquids split. Here its potential has low regularity and vanishes on wells that move with position. Under weak assumptions, they first prove a strong compactness result. With slightly more smoothness, they fully chart the limit behavior through Gamma-convergence. A side result builds shortest paths for a degenerate metric and bounds their length. The work widens the safe ground for messy mixture models.
arxiv-2603-25469: Alvi, Epicoco, and Costa Saura judge wildfire forecast models the way fire crews would. Lab scores for a classifier can flatter a model that cries wolf too often. False alarms carry real cost in daily danger calls. Their method scores both caught fires and false positives in a decision-shaped frame. They run it over a set of learned models. A blend of models catches more real fire and raises fewer false alarms than any single one. The work argues for crew-ready metrics.
arxiv-2603-25669: Wierzchucka and co-authors derive adiabatic equations of state for relativistic plasmas from first principles. For collisional, isotropic plasmas the classic law links pressure to density by a power. Magnetized plasmas without collisions need two pressures, parallel and perpendicular to the field. The authors use the symmetries of the system to get both laws in one framework. In the relativistic case, the double-adiabatic form is not a simple power law. It depends on the pressure anisotropy. The laws cover cases from magnetic mirrors to plasmoids formed in reconnection.
arxiv-2603-25969: Abarajithan and co-authors present FireBridge, a fast way to test hardware and firmware together. Modern accelerators pair complex chips with heavy firmware, and FPGA testing slows each debug round. FireBridge compiles firmware for x86 and bridges it to simulated hardware. The link uses randomized memory bridges and runs in standard simulators. It supports profiling of off-chip data flow and register-level protocol tests. The authors report debug rounds up to fifty times faster than the FPGA flow. Results stayed functionally equal across systolic arrays and CGRAs.
arxiv-2603-26269: Oo and Hartig present a way to trim RML mappings so only the data a query needs gets built. Standard RML work builds the full RDF graph, which wastes time when a query needs just a slice. Their method prunes the mappings while keeping the partial graph able to answer a given SPARQL query in full. On a known benchmark, pruning cuts build time and graph size in a clear way. Query time also drops by a marked amount.
arxiv-2603-26469: Eldenk and Xia present UNIFERENCE, a simulation framework for building and testing distributed AI inference. Work in this area often relies on one-off testbeds, which makes results hard to repeat. UNIFERENCE uses discrete-event simulation with light logical processes that sync only at communication steps. It links with PyTorch Distributed, so the same code can move from simulation to real hardware. In tests it predicts runtime with up to 98.6% accuracy against real deployments, across clusters and edge devices.
arxiv-2603-26569: Cheng, Liu, Li, and Zhang tackle machine unlearning when the data to keep and the data to forget are entangled. Retained samples close to the forget set can be harmed by blunt removal. Their two-phase method first raises loss on the forget set with an augmented Lagrangian step, while sparing loosely related kept data. A second step projects gradients under a Wasserstein-2 penalty to shield close retained samples. Tests across tasks and network types beat prior baselines on both keeping accuracy and removal quality.
arxiv-2603-26869: Granata and co-authors measure how fast stars move inside red galaxies in four Hubble Frontier Fields clusters. The sample holds 723 red member galaxies across the four clusters. Deep MUSE spectroscopy gave direct velocity dispersions for 213 of them, with errors below 5 percent. The team calibrated the Fundamental Plane for early-type members in each cluster. They then assigned dispersions to all 723 galaxies and built the dispersion function for each cluster. The fits agree across clusters, down to low dispersions.
arxiv-2603-27269: Franco and co-authors distill a foundation ECG model into compact classical and quantum students. The teacher, ECGFounder, is fine-tuned for binary classification on PTB-XL and MIT-BIH data. Two classical students, a ResNet-1D and a light CNN, learn from its behavior. A quantum-ready student pairs a convolutional autoencoder with a six-qubit variational circuit. Distillation kept the students competitive while slashing trainable parameters. The teacher still performed best overall on both datasets. Sensitivity tests map the accuracy cost of each compression choice.
arxiv-2603-27469: Ranganath and co-authors compare thirty-three ways to shrink video caches. Self-forcing video models feed their own output back as context. Longer clips thus need far more memory. The study logs 610 prompt-level runs. Two test suites cover short clips and longer stories. One FlowCache-style method stands out for daily use. It squeezes memory about 5.4 times with modest slowdown. Peak memory falls from 19.28 to about 11.7 gigabytes. The most exact methods prove less fit for deployment.
arxiv-2603-27569: Bergach beats Apple's own FFT library on Apple Silicon GPUs. His radix-8 Stockham code hits 138.45 gigaflops at size 4096. That tops the vDSP baseline of 107 gigaflops by 29 percent. A two-tier memory model guides the design. Registers act as the main data tier. Threadgroup memory serves only for exchange. Tests also probe matrix units for butterfly math. Barriers prove cheap, while scattered access is the true bottleneck.
arxiv-2603-27769: Podobryaev finds cut loci for deformed lens space metrics. Lens spaces here carry metrics stretched along Hopf fibers. One parameter family tends toward a sub-Riemannian limit. Geometric control methods locate cut points and times. Those values converge to the known sub-Riemannian ones. Lower bounds for the metric diameter follow. For L(p;1) spaces, the bounds prove exact. Axis symmetry shapes the whole analysis.
arxiv-2603-27869: Ying and co-authors ask when unlabeled data truly help inference. Semi-supervised sets pair few labels with many raw points. Their frame stays lean on premises with many features. A plain debiased method wins only under rate limits. The mean curve must be fit fast enough. Bad mean fits can make raw data harmful. A new method never falls below the supervised baseline. The claim extends to general M-estimation.
arxiv-2603-28069: Clark and ten co-authors give vision-language models a new way to point at things in images and videos. Most models type out coordinates as text, which is slow and hard to learn. MolmoPoint instead picks the visual token that holds the target, then narrows to a subpatch and a spot inside it. The method set records on image pointing tests and open-model GUI pointing. It also improved video pointing and tracking while using far fewer training samples.
arxiv-2603-28569: Yu and co-authors introduce CirrusBench, a benchmark for language model agents in real cloud service work. It is built from authentic cloud service tickets, not synthetic tasks. Those tickets hold long multi-turn logic chains and real tool dependencies. The benchmark also scores customer-focused traits, not just correctness. New metrics cover resolution efficiency and multi-turn latency. Tests find that top models reason well but often struggle with complex real tasks. They also often miss the high efficiency that customer service needs.
arxiv-2603-28769: Mitra presents Spark-LLM-Eval, a distributed framework for evaluating large language models at scale. Older tools handle thousands of cases but struggle at hundreds of thousands or millions. It runs on Apache Spark and treats eval as a data-parallel problem. Every metric includes bootstrap confidence intervals. Model pairs are compared with fit significance tests for each metric type. A content-addressable cache backed by Delta Lake avoids rerunning inference when metric definitions change. Benchmarks show linear scaling with cluster size. The code is open source.
arxiv-2603-28869: Baumann and Rolandi propose an algorithm that solves NP problems in polynomial time, at a steep price. The scheme rests on the many-worlds reading of quantum theory being correct. It also asks the user to wager the fate of all observers in the universe on that bet. The catch is the wager itself, not the running time. If many-worlds fails, the cost falls on every observer at once.
arxiv-2603-29169: Das and co-authors present BLOC, a tool for sparse covariance estimation with non-convex penalties. It works on correlation matrices. An angular Cholesky map turns the hard constraints into a plain box search. That lets a pattern search find global optima, even for rough or black-box losses. Restarts help it escape poor local minima. Each step stays a valid correlation matrix. The team proves convergence and consistency results for the method. In tests, SCAD and MCP penalties beat top rival tools on error and sparsity.
arxiv-2603-29269: Ding and co-authors use machine learning to pin down parameters of magnetized QCD matter. They work within the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model. Two field-dependent quantities are unknown: the coupling and the anomalous magnetic moment ratio. Lattice QCD condensate data serve as ground truth. The NJL gap equation sits inside their network as a physics module. The fitted functions reproduce inverse magnetic catalysis. Both quantities fall smoothly as the magnetic field grows. The work links effective models with lattice data.
arxiv-2603-29769: Esmayli, Koskela, and Nguyen study how much slack quasiconformal maps allow on bad sets. A map counts as quasiconformal when its local stretching stays bounded. Gehring showed the bound may fail on a thin set of codimension one. In metric spaces, a Poincaré condition allows bad sets of codimension p. The authors prove that allowance is sharp. In short, no larger class of bad sets can be permitted in general.
arxiv-2603-29969: Klein and Fivel aim soft logic at Hilbert's sixth problem, the axiomatization of physics. In continuous spaces, each single microstate carries probability zero under classic theory. Their soft numbers give point events tiny infinitesimal chances instead. Soft probability then reads as a fine refinement of the classic notion. They build a Möbius strip from soft numbers as a guiding picture. They also propose an extra axiom for infinitesimal probability. A soft Pascal triangle handles events outside a variable's support.
arxiv-2604-00269: Efraimidis and Hernández bound the harmonic inner radius of any planar domain omitting an open set by the harmonic inner radius of the unit disk. That disk radius is at most three halves. This extends a theorem of Lehtinen from holomorphic functions to harmonic mappings. The paper also provides two related univalence criteria.
arxiv-2604-00569: Zheng and colleagues propose an accelerated proximal bundle method with momentum for convex optimisation. Bundle methods build richer surrogate models than gradient descent, using gradients and function values from many past steps, which speeds and steadies convergence. Yet for smooth convex problems, bundle methods reach only a one-over-k rate, below the optimal one-over-k-squared rate. Adding Nesterov's momentum, the new method reaches the optimal rate under standard assumptions. Numerical tests confirm the method works well.
arxiv-2604-01069: Croft presents smoothed unfolding with cubic B-splines and eigen sifting, after Blobel's plan and a Fortran port into modern form. The method, named Blobel's Regularised Unfolding, differs from histogram methods: the true spread is a smooth function set by spline weights. Smoothing leans on splitting the bend penalty into eigen modes, weighed against data sharpness. He lays out the method's structure, how smoothing strength is set on its own from the data, and matches it with methods including Tikhonov smoothing, Richardson-Lucy steps, and matrix flip.
arxiv-2604-01169: Nelson and colleagues propose a data-driven way to close the gap between simulation and experiment. A generative model first learns from fully observed but imperfect simulation data. It is then lined up with partial but real experimental readings. Applied to atomic positions, the method recovers the target pattern of readings even with several linked observables. Tests on synthetic, molecular, and protein data confirm it works across varied observables.
arxiv-2604-01569: Meng and colleagues launch VideoZeroBench, a long-video benchmark with hand-checked question-answer pairs spanning 13 video domains. Questions target fine-grained cues, fleeting events, and evidence spread across segments, with time spans and key-frame boxes marked. A five-level test plan tests answering with and without evidence hints, joining right answers with time and spatial grounding checked apart. Across 19 models, the best standard QA score is 24.8 percent. No model exceeds a low share when right answers and exact time-and-place finding are jointly needed.
arxiv-2604-01869: Zaytar and colleagues present research on agency primitives for GeoAI aides, linking base models to GIS users' artifact workflows. Advances in space captions, visual questions and promptable segments have not raised output in vector, raster and map work. Model capability alone does not explain the gap; a missing agency layer for joint work does. The authors propose 9 primitives, including routes, sensing, geo-linked memory and dual models, plus a productivity benchmark. They aim for a vocabulary making agentic GIS help usable, testable and matched.
arxiv-2604-02169: Dutta gives a universal fix for distributing graph states over quantum networks. From one elementary two qubit resource state per graph edge, a phase quantum walk step plus local gates, measurements and classical messages builds any target graph state, not just GHZ style states. The key theorem says a Z correction at each node, set by the XOR of far side outcomes on its edges, restores the target for every outcome. The rule is verified on 22 connected graphs, with noise fidelities in closed form and IBM hardware tests confirming it.
arxiv-2604-02369: Yuan and colleagues map agent protocols into three layers: communication, syntactic and semantic. Across 18 protocols, they find mature support for transport, streaming, schemas and lifecycle management, but thin tools for questions, context match and verification. Semantic work thus falls to prompts, wrappers and app specific control logic, creating hidden costs in upkeep and cross system work. The paper names major forms of technical debt and offers guidance for choosing protocols across deployments.
arxiv-2604-02569: García Sarmina, Sun and Dong introduce RFOX, a quantum algorithm for combinatorial optimization that needs no parameter tuning. It pairs a nearly constant non-stoquastic catalyst with a weak counter-diabatic term, keeping the energy gap nearly flat and avoiding the sudden gap collapses of standard drivers. Tests on IBM hardware up to 20 qubits reach near-optimal or exact ground states with up to ten times fewer Trotter slices.
arxiv-2604-02669: Kumar and five colleagues show that language-model bias depends on how it is measured, auditing seven commercial and open-weight models with about 45,000 prompts across nine bias types and seven tasks. On explicit probes models counter stereotypes, but on implicit ones they reproduce them, with gaps up to 0.43 for the same model and groups. Under-studied axes such as caste, language and geography show the strongest stereotyping of all.
arxiv-2604-02769: Yamasaki and three colleagues offer a semiclassical representation of the Hubbard model. The picture uses an unconventional coherent-state form. Treating some dynamical variables as static gives a nonperturbative scheme valid at finite temperature. It captures correlations between sites and extends to systems with many orbitals. Checks against exact one- and two-site solutions match behavior in broad outline, with gaps tied to the smooth character of the density of states. Finite temperature is in scope from the start.
arxiv-2604-02869: Modecrua and three colleagues apply multi-turn reinforcement learning to tool-calling agents. They combine multi-turn group relative policy optimization with generalized token-level policy optimization on customer service tasks. Naive dense per-turn rewards cut performance by up to 14 percentage points through misaligned advantage direction. Their iterative reward calibration designs per-turn rewards from rollout data. It lifts Qwen3-30B-A3B on Tau-Bench airline tasks from 58 to 70 percent. The 4B model rises from 64 to 67 percent.
arxiv-2604-02969: Draca, Matsubara, and Tran build a natural-gradient optimizer for curved parameter spaces that avoids inverting a Fisher matrix. Their method keeps a moving inverse-matrix estimate on the manifold, updating it from new score vectors with low-rank rules, with proven rates for both iterates and estimate. A lean version suits large problems, with tests on variational Bayes, normalizing flows, and reduced-rank regression.
arxiv-2604-03069: Zhang and three colleagues propose SparseSplat, the first feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting model that adapts Gaussian density to scene structure and information richness. Entropy-based sampling places large sparse Gaussians in textureless areas and small dense Gaussians in rich areas. A point cloud network turns local context into splatting attributes, fixing the receptive field mismatch with general optimization. SparseSplat reaches top quality with only 22 percent of the Gaussians, and keeps reasonable quality with only 1.5 percent.
arxiv-2604-03169: Freitas and Leylekian prove that a planar region with one hole can host a first non-trivial Neumann eigenfunction whose nodal line closes fully inside the region. That is the best possible outcome, since a 1956 result bars closed nodal lines on simply connected regions. Part of the argument tracks eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of graph-like regions converging toward metric graphs.
arxiv-2604-03369: Montalto and colleagues release the first public PLATO Input Catalog for the southern long-duration field, LOPS2. Built from Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry plus 3D maps of the local interstellar medium, it lists 217,741 stars, including 202,315 FGK dwarfs and subgiants. The team also estimates reddening for nearly all targets and derives stellar temperatures, radii, and masses uniformly from the observables.
arxiv-2604-03569: Galindo and colleagues' 2026 family of J-affine code kinds results in impure CSS codes for quantum local repair. These quantum codes exceed several bounds that apply to pure quantum local codes, which cover message qudits, distance, length, and reach. They also discuss a link between bounds on quantum local repair and weight-constrained stabilizer codes.
arxiv-2604-03769: Yang Liu and colleagues used fast radio bursts without known distances to weigh in on the Hubble constant, the rate at which the universe expands. Unlocalized bursts are far more common than localized ones, and cosmic expansion leaves its mark on how their dispersion measures spread out. From 2,124 bursts in the CHIME Catalog II, they obtained about 69 kilometers per second per megaparsec, with roughly 22 percent uncertainty. Breaking a tangle with burst energy traits could cut that uncertainty to 9 percent.
arxiv-2604-04169: Coudreuse proves a new estimate for a step-by-step scheme that simulates diffusion equations in one and two dimensions. On simple shapes such as cubes, half-spaces and the torus, his argument rests on a maximum principle for the Hessian determinant of Brenier potentials, applied one step at a time. The result gives density bounds uniform in the time step, and settles the optimality conditions for fast diffusion.
arxiv-2604-04269: Sinha and colleagues track a shift in search tech, from ranking documents toward agents that reason, act and observe over many steps. In such long runs, small early mistakes can snowball, leaving fluent language that masks a mismatch between thought and tool use. This position paper sorts failures seen in work systems across planning, retrieval, reasoning and execution. It calls for checks at each step and holding back under doubt, putting correct process ahead of smooth but unverified completion.
arxiv-2604-04369: Qi, Zhong and Wang formalize DAO-to-DAO payments, where one threshold-run group pays another, optionally hiding the payee, while funds stay under shared control. Their Dao² setup mixes shared key derivation, shared stealth-address generation and threshold ECDSA signing. Plain transfers use a non-stealth address; hidden transfers use a stealth address. The sender threshold-signs, and the payee redeems funds without rebuilding any master secret. Security is proven on paper, and a test anonymous deal for a 7-member DAO ends in under 28 milliseconds with about 2.8 kilobytes.
arxiv-2604-04469: Cacioli tests whether transformer models show scalar variability, where noise grows with magnitude. Gauging hidden-state spread across carriers for 26 values in three 7-8B models, he finds the reverse: variability falls as magnitude rises. The scaling exponent sits near negative 0.19, with no primary layer showing a positive exponent. The anti-scalar pattern runs three to five times stronger along the size axis than on other axes. The findings show distributional learning alone cannot produce scalar spread: they copy log-squeezed size shape but not the noise mark of biology.
arxiv-2604-04669: Majhi, Mondal and Agnihotri host a Birds of a Feather session on healthcare app design in low-resource contexts. There, delivery often depends on community health workers, caregivers and casual care networks. Many healthcare applications assume stable infrastructure, high digital skills and strong institutional support. Building effective apps for such environments requires attention to system limits, local contexts, language diversity and ease-of-use problems. The session offers a forum for discussing design and deployment challenges in poorly served settings, sharing field stories and finding chances for teamwork.
arxiv-2604-05469: Dalla Riva treats language models as evolving organisms and asks when next-token training favors internal models that track the world. He shows optimal prediction error splits into irreducible entropy plus an excess term that vanishes only when the model's encoding preserves the training task's equivalence classes. Frozen dense and mixture-of-experts transformers fit the analysis, in-context learning adds no new distinctions, and per-task adaptation breaks it. Small-model tests confirm the predicted failure modes and rescue paths.
arxiv-2604-05569: Kaasik proves that in Lipschitz-free spaces, three diameter-two traits match their attaining twins. The strong, plain, and local traits each match the twin where extremes are hit, not just neared. The short note joins rough and exact diameter behavior in these spaces, closing the gap between neared and hit extremes.
arxiv-2604-05669: Xie, Zhang, and Li frame machine unlearning statistically, seeking removal of data influence without full retraining. For squared loss their Unlearning Least Squares method proves minimax optimal using only the trained estimator, forget samples, and a small retained subsample. Error splits into an oracle term plus an unlearning cost, and valid inference follows without retraining.
arxiv-2604-05969: Acharya and Gupta build MCPSHIELD, a formal security frame for AI agents that use the Model Context Protocol to reach tools and data. From a scan of over 177,000 tools they sort threats into 7 groups and 23 attack paths across four surfaces, and model tool chains with trust-boundary checks. No lone defense tops 34 percent coverage, while their layered design claims 91 percent in theory.
arxiv-2604-06369: Ambrus reviews planned power tuning for tight railways, where heavy freight beside fast riders strains AC traction networks. Costly builds make software energy plans a possible option. Single-train tuning misses the coupled electrical interactions that set capacity on mixed-traffic networks. Multi-train TTP simulations capture those interactions, but their algorithms trade tractability against flexibility. Predictive and distributed methods narrow that trade, yet fidelity and real-time operation at scale appear separately. Finally, optimal speed profiles differ from executable ones, especially under human drivers rather than Automatic Train Operation.
arxiv-2604-06469: Moghaddami and four colleagues predict Alzheimer's progression from resting-state scans with a history-aware graph neural network. Alzheimer's affects over seven million Americans, has no cure, yet early detection may slow it. Their model predicts moves to a more severe stage at the next visit. Connectivity graphs from 303 subjects' resting-state scans feed the model, whose recurrent block reads full visit histories and handles irregular gaps through distance features. It reaches 82.9 percent accuracy overall and about 69 percent on normal-to-mild conversions despite missing visits.
arxiv-2604-06569: Cheng and Zhang expose a flaw in cancer ecDNA research: benchmarks leaked the answer into their features, sharply inflating scores. Their replacement framework, ECLIPSE, predicts ecDNA status from ordinary genomic features alone, scoring 812 out of 1,000 on the AUROC scale. It models shifting dynamics with physics-constrained neural equations, and uses causal reasoning to flag treatment weaknesses with eightyfold enrichment over chance. The lesson is that careful methods beat fancier architectures in high-stakes biomedical machine learning.
arxiv-2604-06769: Borscz and four colleagues simulate suprathermal enhancement in fusion fuels. Fast particles in dense plasmas can shift burn at confinement regimes. Their Monte Carlo code weighs fast-fusion gains in DT, deuterium, and boron fuels, with stopping powers and anisotropic scattering. Earlier hopes for suprathermal criticality in pure deuterium prove overstated tenfold, with no regime sustaining a chain reaction. Only DT shows a critical regime without neutron leakage. Fast protons peak near 4 MeV in 11BH3 fuel, fast-fusion energy stays below 40 percent, and an alpha-driven avalanche is ruled out.
arxiv-2604-06969: Revilla and 19 colleagues find planet-induced cyclic shifts of star action in GJ 436, a low-mass star with a Neptune-sized planet in a polar off-center orbit. From 18 years of sharp optical spectra, they find action signs raised at the planet orbital period, shaped by stellar spin and the star's 8-year field cycle. They read this as a star-planet field link. With a shape model they match these periods if the planet holds a field of 6 to 110 Gauss.
arxiv-2604-07069: Zakwan and four colleagues build a control method for non linear systems that uses structured state space models as stand in models. Such models track long term links in time series data with work that grows in a straight line, unlike transformers whose work grows with the square of length. The paper first checks whether these models can be steered and watched, then designs controls with matrix inequalities based on contraction theory. A split rule lets watchers and controllers be designed apart while keeping the loop stable.
arxiv-2604-07169: Cui and four colleagues present FLUID, a reusable framework for tracking and smoothing hidden states in nonlinear dynamical systems. Older deep methods often rebuild their maps at every new observation, wasting work. FLUID instead trains one recurrent summary network plus two conditional flow models on simulated trajectories, then reuses them across observation sequences. Tests on advection-diffusion, Burgers, and Lorenz systems show accurate filtering and smoothing, with errors tracked beyond the training horizon.
arxiv-2604-07269: Li, Du, and Guo build SEA, a diagnostic agent that learns from experience instead of treating each case in isolation. Its dual-memory module stores reusable diagnostic patterns, and a reinforcement-training framework jointly tunes reasoning and memory management. On a standard benchmark, SEA reaches 92.46 percent accuracy, beating the strongest baseline by 19.6 points. On a long-horizon set, it also finishes best, and expert review finds its consolidated rules clinically sound, useful, and trustworthy.
arxiv-2604-07369: Patel and three colleagues test how emotional tone in prompts steers large language models. Past work used single positive tones, leaving strength and negative tones untested. They build human- and model-made prompts across joy, encouragement, anger, and insecurity at varied strengths, plus a gold set where human and model labels match. Positive tones give more accurate and less toxic answers, but they also raise flattery, where the model praises rather than corrects.
arxiv-2604-07469: Cao and five colleagues test sequenced AI feedback, which gives hints before answers, against direct feedback in 199 students. Sequenced feedback raised engagement a bit and felt more encouraging and autonomy-supporting, but it also raised mental effort. A good mood pathway from encouragement was fully cancelled by a bad behavior pathway tied to tasks needing three or more tries. Net learning was significantly poorer with sequenced feedback, a caution for feedback design.
arxiv-2604-07569: Conklin and seven colleagues argue large language models are best seen as lossy compression. Over training, models keep only training-data facts that serve their goals. Pre-training yields models optimally compressed for next-sequence prediction, near the Information Bottleneck bound on compression. Across open-weights models, each compresses in its own way, likely due to data and training-recipe differences. Yet across model families, compression optimality and information content predict downstream scores across many benchmarks, linking how models store facts to how well they perform.
arxiv-2604-07669: Li and six colleagues offer MolReAct, which recasts compound tuning as search over reaction spaces put forward by a tool-boosted language model. Old synth-aware methods explore a large space of changes from reaction patterns and bought blocks, a search that grows harder when trait gains need multiple steps. At each step, the model joins prior chem knowledge with chem tools to find a set of reactions. Across tasks, MolReAct hits the highest Top-10 score in 11 of 14 tasks and the best speed on 12 of 14 tasks.
arxiv-2604-07969: Fountzoulas presents Kathleen, a text classification system that works directly on raw UTF-8 bytes with frequency-domain processing. It needs no tokenizer, no attention mechanism, and under 470,000 parameters. Recurrent oscillator banks use damped sine-wave convolutions with time memory for linear-time sequence work. An FFT-Rotate wavetable encoder maps all 256 byte values with a single learnable vector. Phase harmonics add a sine-wave nonlinearity with just six learnable phase values, and further modules add content-dependent memory and sequencing.
arxiv-2604-08369: In a 2026 paper, Sethi presents TrACE, a training free controller that spends computing power on language model agents only where decisions look hard. At each step it samples a few candidate moves and checks how often the model agrees with itself. Strong agreement ends the step at once, while weak agreement buys more samples up to a set cap before the majority move wins. TrACE matched fixed budget rivals in accuracy while using far fewer model calls on reasoning and household navigation tests.
arxiv-2604-08469: Wang, Nigmetov, and Morozov add local shape information to neural networks through persistence based data augmentation. Their method encodes gradient flow regions and their layered growth with the Morse Smale complex, keeping local topology across scales instead of summarizing it globally. Tests on tissue image classification and porous material regression beat baselines and global shape summaries, while pruning the base layer cuts memory with little performance loss.
arxiv-2604-08769: Kim and eleven colleagues present the ice list of young star EC 53 from JWST spectra spanning 1.6 to 28 microns in quiescent and burst phases. After clearing the dust signal, they fit water ice and break down ammonia, carbon dioxide, methanol, carbon monoxide, and methane against lab shapes. No ice band changes clearly between phases, so short bursts leave the shell ices largely the same, while amounts exceed typical hidden young stars.
arxiv-2604-09469: Gropper, Ueki, and Wang carry a classic number-theory result into topology. They prove a 3-manifold analogue of the Neukirch-Uchida theorem, which recovers a number field from its absolute Galois group. Infinite links with a Chebotarev density property play the role of the primes. The absolute Galois group of a manifold is built from finite sublink complements. Two branched covers of the 3-sphere match exactly when their Galois groups match via a characteristic-preserving isomorphism.
arxiv-2604-09569: Bodonhelyi and nine colleagues review and benchmark mind-wandering detection in online education, where minds drift about 30 percent of the time. Progress has lagged amid mixed methods, varied data prep, and inconsistent metrics. The team builds one shared pipeline tuned to each signal type. It spans EEG, facial video, eye tracking, and body signals across 14 datasets. Thirteen traditional and neural models, including federated learning, are tested on every dataset. A post-probe test explores how learners re-engage after drifting, through re-reading or re-watching.
arxiv-2604-09869: García Sarmina and four co-authors present Q-PIPE, a method loading standard data into quantum states, writing values into oracle phases, turned by phase guessing. Sums and gaps come from stepwise oracle calls, with no quantum math circuits. Applied to image edge finding by aimed finite gaps, the oracle needs gated-NOT gates scaling with pixels and guessing qubits, matching tuned novel boosted quantum form setup. Evenly gated build cuts depth 53 to 59 times and preserves edge structure under device noise, with match 0.99 against the standard gradient.
arxiv-2604-10069: Yoshida, Fukumoto, and Yamamoto speed up holographic data storage with a new recording method. A micromirror device shows each data page while a focused line beam scans it. The recording medium and a spherical reference wave move in step with the scan. Removing the stop-and-go drive motion allows rapid, continuous, multiplexed recording. Partial holograms still rebuild the full page at once through the reference wave. Tests gave a bit error rate below 10 percent at a 5 millisecond exposure, with stable recording at 150 hertz.
arxiv-2604-10169: Duan, Gao, Xian, and Shi predict multi-agent trajectories for autonomous driving with MAVEN-T, a distillation framework. A teacher combines a graph encoder with shifted-window spatial attention and a mixture-of-experts head for maneuver futures. A compact student learns from its teacher at feature, attention, and semantic levels, then refines with policy optimization rewards for safety, comfort, and progress. Across five driving data sets, it uses about six times fewer parameters, runs nearly four times faster, and hits 14.6 millisecond latency on a Jetson AGX Orin.
arxiv-2604-10269: Pham and Vu show a tree's independence complex is contractible exactly when truncation moves at branching points reduce it to a path P_n with n congruent to 1 modulo 3. The independence complex encodes a tree's independent sets as simplices, and contractible means it can shrink to a point. Truncation moves prune the tree at branching points, step by step, until only the path remains. As a consequence, they also characterize trees whose independence polynomial at minus 1 equals 1 or minus 1.
arxiv-2604-10369: Dabrowski, Jonsson, Ordyniak, Osipov, and Wahlström close the map for near solvable modular equations. Each equation links at most a few unknowns modulo m, and the goal drops the fewest equations to reach solvability. The prime power case for two unknowns per equation had stayed open until now. Their balanced subgraph covering method puts that case in fixed parameter tractable form. A matching lower bound under ETH pins the factor set by prime factor count as best possible.
arxiv-2604-10469: Su, Ye, Wang, Guo, and Liu give subagging an exact finite sample variance split. Standard 63 percent subsample shares long served as defaults with no exact backing. Their Hoeffding ANOVA split works for any symmetric learner with no smooth limits. Subagging acts as a low pass filter, keeping low order signals while shrinking high order noise by powers. A complexity tuned sampler then beats fixed shares by matching the cut to learner complexity.
arxiv-2604-10569: Wettenstein, Nadel, and Boker speed up Background SHAP for deep decision-tree ensembles. SHAP rates each feature's contribution by comparing against background data. Earlier fast methods hit a preprocessing wall that grows as 3 to the power of depth. Their WoodelfHD extension cuts that factor to 2 to the power of depth with a Strassen-like scheme and merged path nodes. It handles trees up to depth 21. It runs 33 times faster than the rival at depth 12 and 162 times faster at depth 15.
arxiv-2604-10669: Antonelli and three colleagues introduce LTLF, a temporal logic for event series that states event frequencies. New measure-sensitive operators let the logic work out frequencies and predict future events, helping watch and control quantitative systems like machine-learning classifiers. New modal quantifiers with standard Kripke-style semantics state event-series properties in one structure and link seen frequencies to ideal distributions. The design bridges formal logical thought and seen data.
arxiv-2604-10769: Majumder, Yu, and Xie show that workload mix shapes grid-facing power dynamics in shared-GPU AI data centers. As inference share rises, total power variability traces a U-shape while short-horizon ramping traces a hump, with sizes and turning points depending on system load. A trace-calibrated design linking arrivals, queueing, scheduling, and GPU power reveals an asymmetric mechanism: at middle mixes, queued batch jobs fill idle capacity left by fluctuating inference demand. Yet short-horizon ramping stays high because inference swings feed straight into realized power.
arxiv-2604-11069: Al-Dweik and two colleagues derive exact outage chance and ergodic capacity for the near user in two-user downlink NOMA. Noise and fading become linked after successive interference cancellation, so exact study uses joint curves of post-cancellation noise and fading. The derived curves evaluate rest interference well and yield an exact closed-form formula for near-user outage and a single-integral expression for capacity. Unlike existing work, the formulae are parameter-free, giving more accurate testing.
arxiv-2604-11369: Tun, Dong, and Pavlogiannis introduce AtomSanitizer, a faster algorithm for testing conflict serializability in concurrent programs. Atomicity violations cause many concurrency bugs, and the best existing testers run in time O(nk cubed) and O(nk times k plus v plus ell). AtomSanitizer runs in O(nk squared) in streaming style with less memory, and is built for minimal locking. Benchmarks show it beats existing testers, and a TSAN implementation adds minimal overhead over the data-race engine, making it the first tester suited to runtime monitoring.
arxiv-2604-11569: El Asal and Mahboub study finite generation in polynomial semirings, treating polynomials in α with whole-number coefficients as an additive monoid for real algebraic α. In the atomic case, atoms are powers of α up to a bound, and finite generation hinges on the minimal polynomial's divisibility by a negative-tail form. They fully characterize minimal polynomials differing from another polynomial by a whole-number constant. They also show finite generation forces α to be a weak Perron number, then apply the theory to cubic polynomials and rank-3 monoids.
arxiv-2604-11669: Segarra and six colleagues present Nanvix, a multikernel OS for dense serverless deployments. Providers pack many applications per host, but density must not weaken performance or isolation, and naive sharing creates contention. Nanvix splits short-lived per-invocation state from persistent state shared within a tenant. Applications run in a user VM with a micro-kernel, forwarding I/O to a system VM with a shared macro-kernel. The split gives isolation across tenants, cuts contention, and yields order-of-magnitude faster startups with I/O overhead.
arxiv-2604-11869: Motta, Neto, Prather, and Cárdenas-Avendaño use Jipole, a radiative transfer code, to compute how black hole images from magnetohydrodynamic simulations respond to model settings. Those pixel-wise sensitivities form a Jacobian mapping settings to image space. In mock tests, the fitting landscape proves structured, with anisotropies and local minima, yet gradient guidance keeps exploration tractable. Gradients still guide recovery well under idealised, blurred, and noisy conditions.
arxiv-2604-12069: Zhang and five colleagues propose a black-box evaluation for token-level explanations in language systems, where API-only access blocks explainers. They measure top-token flip rate under perturbations — swapping, deletion, shuffling, and back-translation. Across three datasets and six encoder and decoder models, with 64,800 cases, decoders prove more stable than encoder baselines, with 73 percent lower flip rates. Stability improves with scale, gaining 44 percent from 7B to 70B. Relating scores to inference cost yields a cost tradeoff curve for predeployment model selection.
arxiv-2604-12269: Sergey Dyachenko and two colleagues analyze the stability of steep Stokes waves on deep water. They are periodic traveling waves, studied as steepness grows. The tallest wave has a peaked profile. The team derives criteria and normal forms for four bifurcations that repeat in turn. They are new figure-eight bands, their collapse to vertical slopes, and new circular bands. Reconnection of figure-infinity bands completes the set. Numerical checks for the first two cycles match the theory closely.
arxiv-2604-12369: Stephen Wiggins derives a formula linking quantum scrambling to unstable periodic orbits. Scrambling is the spread of quantum information through a system. Out-of-time-order correlators measure that spread. His semiclassical expansion sums over orbits on a special invariant surface near a saddle point. A local instability exponent governs the growth. When observation times match orbit periods, growth simplifies to one and a half times that exponent. The pattern could guide selective control of scrambling.
arxiv-2604-12469: Lingfang Li and Procheta Sen study how noise in fine-tuning data shapes language model learning. They test three noise types across three model families and three tasks. Label noise corrupts answers, while grammatical and typographical noise corrupt wording. Label noise causes the largest performance drops by far. Grammar and typo noise sometimes help slightly, acting as regularization. Noise effects concentrate in task-specific layers. Attention structures stay comparatively stable throughout.
arxiv-2604-12869: Riccardo Consonni and Luca Magri explain extreme events with a three-stage cascade. A slow regime holds fast vectors tangent to fast directions. A transition regime turns fast eigenvalues neutrally stable and breaks tangency. A critical regime opens a strong spectral gap, aligning vectors along the dominant fast direction. Two precursors built on this cascade forewarn extreme events and critical transitions. Tests on low- and higher-dimensional systems give perfect precision and recall. The work opens a path to time-forecasting extreme events from theory.
arxiv-2604-12969: Yubraj Bhandari and three colleagues generate abdominal anatomy with set organ sizes. Phantoms aid imaging research but lack controlled variation. AbdomenGen synthesizes organ masks in sequence, conditioning on the body mask and earlier organs. A Volume Control Scalar decouples organ size from body habitus for clear volume control. Liver dice reaches about five sixths, calibration holds across minus three to plus three, and organs modulate independently. Wasserstein-based selection cuts training data distance by 73.6 percent in a liver-enlargement cohort.
arxiv-2604-13269: Nadeem, Wilcox, and Lee compute the charged kaon electric polarizability from four-point functions in lattice QCD, the Euclidean analog of low-energy Compton bounce. The polarizability splits into an elastic term from the charge radius, via the kaon EM form factor, and an inelastic term from time-integrated gaps of four-point correlation functions. From 500 Wilson quenched lattice samples they obtain polarizability 1.682 plus or minus 0.523 times 10 to the minus 4 cubic femtometers. The squared charge radius is 0.3303 plus or minus 0.0028 square femtometers, shifted to the physical pion mass.
arxiv-2604-13569: Tian and four colleagues simulate the non X-ray background facing DIXE, a proposed high-resolution survey of hot Milky Way gas aboard the China Space Station. With a detailed Geant4 mass model, they track cosmic rays, albedo neutrons, and albedo photons through the instrument, plus a delayed glow left by protons trapped over the South Atlantic Anomaly. That delayed glow fades to negligible levels within about five minutes of leaving the anomaly.
arxiv-2604-13669: Canizo, Garriz, and Marin pin down the long-time behavior of heat flow in hyperbolic space. Heat spreads differently in curved space than on a flat plane. They give precise speeds of convergence in L1 and L-infinity to asymptotic profiles, adapting entropy estimates to curved, non-compact spaces. For L1 initial data, the profile is not universal. It remembers the initial distribution of mass. Transient profiles, treated as minimizers of the entropy functional, carry the space's geometric information and drive the proof.
arxiv-2604-13869: Salomaa, Keski-Vakkuri, and Nadal-Gisbert study how to harvest entanglement from the quantum vacuum with some detectors per side. Perturbation theory shows the leading negativity comes from a small submatrix. Its size grows only linearly with detector count. For three-detector setups and symmetric four-detector setups they derive exact results and name the best layouts. In a linear chain, harvested entanglement grows linearly with detector number.
arxiv-2604-13969: Chakraborty, Singh, and Jaiswal build a 3D memory-on-memory compute-in-memory architecture that runs general matrix operations, not just dot products. SRAM-eDRAM hybrid crossbars in 22-nanometer technology handle transpose, element-wise addition, and multiplication at 4-bit precision. A transpose-based design plus peripheral-aware layout balances latency, energy, and compute density while staying compatible with standard dot-product CIM.
arxiv-2604-14369: Wei, von Oppen, and Glazman build an analytic theory of quasiparticle lifetime and spectra in the twisted-bilayer-graphene Mott semimetal. In the topological heavy fermion picture, weak mixing between c- and f-electrons pours Berry curvature into a flat f-band. Recasting the flat-band problem as on-site Hubbard physics on non-orthogonal orbitals, they compute the Green's function by an equation-of-motion method. Low-energy quasiparticles emerge whose spread and decay scale with interaction strength, staying sharp in energy and momentum near the Fermi level.
arxiv-2604-14669: Song and five colleagues characterize when gradient-free zeroth-order methods stay stable while training deep networks, using the standard two-point gradient estimate. Unlike first-order methods, whose stability hinges only on the largest Hessian eigenvalue, mean-square stability here depends on the whole Hessian spectrum. Since that spectrum cannot be computed in practice, they derive usable bounds from the top eigenvalue and the trace alone. Experiments found full-batch zeroth-order methods sitting at the predicted stability edge, with large steps quietly regularizing the trace.
arxiv-2604-14969: Dai and four others present AC/DC, using coevolution for large language model discovery. Current training restarts runs with static data or rewards when new skills are wanted. AC/DC evolves models by merging and tasks by synthetic making, growing sets surpassing larger models using less GPU memory. Populations cover expertise more broadly than curated models or baselines, without explicit benchmark optimization. Coverage improves over time, tasks and models innovate continually, and best-of-N selection improves, showing coevolution discovers broader capabilities from base models.
arxiv-2604-15069: Hu, Gauthier, and Naima replace the usual Laplacian matrix in graph neural nets with a doubly stochastic matrix. Built from the inverse of a modified Laplacian, the new matrix encodes multi-step closeness and local centrality. Exact inversion is too costly, so a cut-off Neumann series approximates it, forming the DsmNet model. A compensation step feeds lost mass back into self-loops, restoring strict row-stochasticity.
arxiv-2604-15169: Berezowski, Hassanzadeh, and Ginde map thirteen papers from 2015 to 2025 on predicting downhole drilling metrics from surface data. The review names eight common surface metrics and seven downhole targets, with neural nets dominating current methods. No study yet tries masked autoencoder foundation models, despite their strength on time-series tasks. The authors call these models a feasible but untested opportunity, urging head-to-head validation against existing methods.
arxiv-2604-15369: Ma and five colleagues build a locally run agentic workflow that finds personal details in crash narratives, where sparse and uneven names, addresses, and plate numbers block wider safety research. A hybrid extractor routes structured items to rules and tricky items to a fine-tuned model, with ensemble extraction and an evidence-based verifier filtering false hits. On real crash data it beats baselines, reaching precision 0.82, recall 0.94, and accuracy 0.96.
arxiv-2604-15669: Lesmana and three colleagues build EvoSK, a setup where agents learn on a rugged spin-glass map and the worst are swapped out. The setup tunes itself to the brink where frozen order sets in, with burst sizes that follow a power law near minus 1.5 and payoffs that top any fixed setup. At this brink, two kinds of order merge: only the heavy tail of the burst sizes gives the slow falloff that the tug between choice and change needs.
arxiv-2604-15769: Guo, Wu, and Yiu give the first expressivity theory for spiking self-attention. Leaky fire-and-integrate nets match any order-free map, with a side-stop net for softmax settling as one over root T. Spike-count floors say near misses need L_f squared n d over epsilon squared spikes. Widths of 47 to 89 on CIFAR and ImageNet say why 4 steps do, though worst-case calls for 10,000 or more. Tests on Spikformer, QKFormer, and SpikingResformer back predictions at R squared 0.97.
arxiv-2604-16269: Escorza and six co-authors benchmark current-to-voltage circuits for quantum transport tests. Good amplification matters when measuring current flow through atomic and tiny junctions, where currents span a huge range. They design and compare four designs: logarithmic, single-stage linear, series-linear, and multi-stage, tuned for break junction methods. Each is judged on sharpness, noise, and dynamic range, yielding trade-offs and useful tips for choice in quantum transport experiments.
arxiv-2604-16469: Song proposes B-PASTE, a method to cut waiting time for language-model agents that alternate reasoning and tool use. Earlier speculative execution guessed single future tool calls, but B-PASTE guesses bounded branches of future work, ranking them by critical-path savings, not raw likelihood. Only high-value branch starts run on spare resources, with checks for interference, downstream value and state safety. On Thor-class edge hardware, early tests showed up to 1.4 times end-to-end speed, even under tight resource budgets.
arxiv-2604-16669: Kebande opens stringology-based cryptology, using string tools on cipher outputs. Modern ciphers make lots of sequential data: keystreams, cipher blocks and hash outputs. Old checks rely on random tests and algebra attacks. Reading outputs as symbol strings, string tools spot repeat patterns, substring spreads and structural links. Pattern counts and substring repeat scores test keystream outputs from stream ciphers. Tests show the approach adds fresh insight into cipher sequence structure and may aid future structural attacks.
arxiv-2604-16869: Daryanoosh studies open quantum systems, whose evolution forgets its past, and describes their generators with two numbers: dissipative strength and non-normality. Normal generators split cleanly into decaying and norm-preserving parts. Non-normal ones, by contrast, can briefly amplify signals, which magnifies errors and raises the cost of quantum simulation.
arxiv-2604-17169: Khennoufa and five colleagues propose two-tier high-altitude stations that harvest energy from nearby platforms' signals. Regular stations act as base stations, while a mother station links them to the ground station, enabling wireless energy transfer. The team derives optimal station placement, formulates a joint placement and harvesting optimization solved in steps, and checks it with Q-learning. Both approaches beat conventional harvesting systems on data rate, with Q-learning ahead on linear models after intensive training.
arxiv-2604-17269: Saxena, Jaryal, and Sharma study quasinormal modes of the JMN naked singularity using exact WKB analysis. In the complex radial plane, they construct the WKB momentum function and Stokes geometry for frequencies. They find bow-shaped Stokes curves near the central singularity, showing it stems from the logarithmic branch-point singularity of the WKB phase at the center, absent in Schwarzschild spacetime. That topology thus marks the naked singularity in the perturbation equation's global structure, showing WKB analysis can probe compact objects and distinguish black holes from horizonless alternatives.
arxiv-2604-17469: Redig and van Tol study swings in a boundary-driven harmonic model, a system held out of equilibrium by its edges. Its steady state mixes products of geometric distributions whose local settings follow uniform order statistics. For such states the authors prove a law of large numbers, a central limit theorem, and large-deviation results for broad classes of local measures, generalizing the density field. They also gauge how far the system sits from local equilibrium.
arxiv-2604-17669: Ciubotariu and colleagues present a full review of the NTIRE 2026 Low Light Image Enhancement Challenge, on entries and final results. The challenge seeks networks making clearer, eye-catching images in diverse, hard settings, fixing information lost to low contrast and noise. A total of 195 entrants signed up for the first track and 153 for the second, with 22 teams sending valid entries in the end. The review rates state-of-the-art gains in joint noise removal and low-light work, showing big field progress on a novel dataset.
arxiv-2604-17869: Chu and two colleagues probe sub-GeV dark matter with paleo-detectors, ancient minerals that record particle tracks over geological timescales. Cosmic-ray boosts or production inside core-collapse supernovae can push slow dark matter to near-light speeds. That yields nuclear recoils above detector thresholds. Using olivine at 100 gram-gigayear exposure, they project 95 percent confidence limits on dark matter-nucleon cross sections. The masses run from a few MeV to hundreds of MeV, with sensitivity gains of orders of magnitude over conventional searches.
arxiv-2604-18069: Leixin Zhang and Coltekin propose Socio-Contrastive Learning, a method that models both annotator perspectives and socio-demographic representations. Past work usually looks at one demographic factor at a time, yet real perspectives grow from complex social contexts, and finer attributes explain them better. Their method combines social features with text to predict perspectives, beating standard concatenation methods. The learned codes also support study and display of how demographic factors relate to perspective gaps.
arxiv-2604-18469: Sievers and Roozbehani extend the synthetic control method for baseline gauging in demand-response power markets. These numbers decide payouts, yet machine learning predicts weakly and causal methods stay rarely used. The classical version fits the treated unit from same-day donors but ignores time-based structure in leftovers. The extended version adds outside signals, lagged treated load, and lagged donor signals, catching echo effects, delayed replies, and error fixes. Ausgrid smart-meter tests beat the classical version and strong benchmarks, most through dynamic add-ons.
arxiv-2604-18769: Troyanov studies the inner vertex isoperimetric problem on regular trees, finding the exact isoperimetric profile for finite connected sets. He introduces a boundary invariant called the boundary branching excess, which gives a simple criterion for optimality. A set is optimal exactly when this excess stays below a threshold set by the tree degree. Every set also admits a canonical decomposition as an iterated gluing of full sets, whose entire boundary consists of leaves, yielding a complete account of all minimizers.
arxiv-2604-19069: Mathew presents Product-of-Experts training, which discounts examples where biased models are overconfident. A hypothesis-only model still scores 57.7 percent on SNLI, showing strong spurious correlations, and about 39 percent of baseline errors trace to artifacts. It nearly preserves accuracy at about 89 percent while cutting bias reliance, with bias agreement falling from about 50 percent to 45 percent. An ablation finds lambda of one and a half best trades debiasing against accuracy. Behavioral tests still show negation and numerical reasoning issues.
arxiv-2604-19269: Wang and colleagues propose CS3, a framework that strengthens two-tower retrievers, the lightweight models that first shortlist candidates in recommender systems, without breaking real-time limits. It adds self-revision inside each tower through adaptive feature denoising, plus mutual awareness between towers for better alignment. It also reuses downstream model knowledge for cross-stage consistency. Tests on three public datasets show steady gains over strong baselines, and the system has been deployed in a large advertising service.
arxiv-2604-19369: Weigand and colleagues introduce IonMorphNet, a model for peak picking in mass spectrometry imaging that learns ion image shapes without task-specific supervision.
